h1: GHRP-6 peptide: what the endocrine studies and the Cuban stroke trial measured, why it makes you hungry, and what was never tested
dek: The first growth hormone releasing peptide, from 1984, with a real literature: single-dose hormone studies, a diagnostic test validated in 250 people, and a phase 3 stroke trial of a fixed combination. None of it is about muscle or fat. This page tables the studies, explains the hunger and the cortisol, and says what the three-times-daily injection pattern rests on.

What people report outside the literature
queries.boundary: Forum reports describe intense hunger within minutes, water retention, tiredness and a warm flush, with three-times-daily injection for months. None of the studies used that pattern, and none measured what months of ghrelin-receptor stimulation does.

queries.heading: Side effects: cortisol, prolactin, hunger, and what was never measured
queries.boundary: Cortisol and prolactin rise with GHRP-6 in the studies that measured them, more than with ipamorelin; hunger is its signature. Beyond single-dose endocrine work and one 7-day stroke trial, no safety data exist for the way it is used.

queries.heading: Why does GHRP-6 cause hunger?
queries.answer: Because it is a ghrelin mimic. Ghrelin is the stomach's hunger hormone, and GHRP-6 was the compound that led to the discovery of its receptor; activating that receptor in the hypothalamus drives food intake, which is why a 2025 mouse study chose GHRP-6 as the tool to engage the brain's ghrelin system and why hunger is the first thing users report. The effect is the mechanism, not a side effect of it.

What is GHRP-6?
queries.answer: GHRP-6 is a six-amino-acid synthetic peptide (His-D-Trp-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2) described by Cyril Bowers in 1984, the first growth hormone releasing peptide. It acts on the ghrelin receptor to make the pituitary release growth hormone, and its discovery led to the identification of that receptor and of ghrelin itself. It has been used as a research tool and a diagnostic test agent, never approved as a medicine, and is sold as a research chemical.

queries.heading: What is the half-life of GHRP-6?
queries.answer: Short. A 2013 pharmacokinetic study gave nine men single intravenous boluses of 100, 200 and 400 micrograms per kilogram and found a two-phase decline with the peptide still measurable at 12 hours; the half-life figures are in the full text, not the abstract. The growth hormone pulse it triggers lasts about an hour, which is why the community injects it several times a day.

queries.heading: Does GHRP-6 increase weight?
queries.answer: No human study has measured body weight or composition after GHRP-6. It increases hunger, which is why the community expects weight gain and why a 2025 mouse study found intranasal GHRP-6 increased food intake; whether the growth hormone pulses change body composition in people has never been tested.

information_gain: The only page that tables GHRP-6's human studies by what was given and measured, showing that they are single intravenous doses measuring growth hormone, ACTH and cortisol, a 250-person validation of the GHRH plus GHRP-6 diagnostic test, one oral and nasal sleep study, and a 188-patient Cuban phase 3 stroke trial of GHRP-6 with EGF that found no difference in disability; that says no human study in the ledger gave it subcutaneously, the only route it is sold for, or measured weight, muscle or fat; that explains hunger as the mechanism (a ghrelin mimic that led to the receptor's discovery) rather than a side effect; and that separates GHRP-6 from GHRP-2, which is approved in Japan as a diagnostic agent, and from the antagonist [D-Lys3]-GHRP-6 that the drafter's search pulled in.
serp_format_rewarded: Explainer. A wiki guide and a 1997 paper rank; a cited page with a study table and a plain mechanism section fits.
